memory_candidates.content: When a repo-wide lint/gate script that runs in a multi-repo agent-system (deployed into many consumer repos of differing layout) enumerates a fixed list of this repo's own directories, it silently degrades to zero coverage in every other repo -- the defect is invisible because the script still exits 0/PASS. The general default: enumerate via `git ls-files` (repo-wide, gitignore-respecting) minus one documented exempt set, never a hard-coded directory list. This generalizes beyond task-reference linting to any cross-repo lint/gate script.

A test fixture that must invoke a script requiring deploy-root-guard.sh (parent-of-parent directory literally .claude or .opencode, no REPO_ROOT override) cannot construct a scenario where BOTH systems are literally absent from disk, because the fixture must place the runner's own copy inside one of them. When a plan specifies such a literal-both-absent test case for a script with this constraint, the closest achievable equivalent is: host the runner in a payload-free tree, invoke targeting only the genuinely-absent sibling system, and document the substitution explicitly rather than silently narrowing or skipping the assertion.
